subject: Urgent: MetroHealth production latency & 5xx spike — AZ1 containment
messages:
From: Carla Rodriguez <carla.rodriguez@metrohealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@metrohealth.com
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Spike in errors and latency impacting claims API

Sean —

We’re seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and tail latency for our claims API routed through your AZ1 endpoint (region: us-west). Error rate jumped to ~8% over the last 12 minutes and p95 latency is ~1.8s (normal ~120ms). This is affecting critical patient claims flows for three large hospital customers (code red). Our monitoring shows a correlated increase in Redis KV timeouts and a build-up of requests queued at the gateway.

We’ve opened a ticket with our cloud provider but need immediate help from Redwood to stabilize traffic and avoid ongoing SLA breaches. Can you:
- Confirm you see the same metrics on your side
- Shift traffic off the affected AZ1 while you triage (we can accept retries to eastus2 or westus3)
- Provide a tentative recovery ETA and what mitigations you’ll apply

Attaching our last-minute error snapshot and links to our dashboards. Please escalate to your SRE and exec team. This is impacting live revenue-critical flows; we’ll need a direct line (phone/bridge).

—Carla
Carla Rodriguez
Head of Platform Operations, MetroHealth
carla.rodriguez@metrohealth.com

Attachments: error_snapshot_2028-12-04.json (stub), perf-az1-5xx-20281204.png (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carla Rodriguez <carla.rodriguez@metrohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: Spike in errors and latency impacting claims API

Ben / Marissa / Hannah —

Seen and escalating. I confirm matching telemetry on our side: AZ1 p95 latency 1.6–2.0s, 5xx rate ~7.5% across the MetroHealth routing group. KV cache miss storms and request queue growth on the local frontends are evident.

Immediate action (please act now, I want a war room):
1) Marissa — activate the AZ failover runbook for MetroHealth (Playbook: AZ1-containment-v2). Start transparent routing to eastus2/westus3. Prefer split-weighted approach to avoid mass failover churn.
2) Ben — spin up customer-facing comms and a dedicated bridge (Bluejeans bridge started; details below). Provide a short messaging template to Carla (ETA 15m).
3) Hannah — check autoscale headroom on the dedicated pool and confirm whether priority pin is blocking traffic movement. If the priority pin exists, coordinate a temporary lift for MetroHealth exec-approved flows.
4) All — capture a short timeline and save logs/trace IDs for legal/compliance.

Proposed immediate routing change: shift 60% of MetroHealth traffic off AZ1 (30% eastus2, 30% westus3) and keep 40% to AZ1 for graceful KV warmup. If errors fall <1% in 10m, continue progressive shift. If errors persist, full drain.

Bridge: https://bluejeans.redwood.ai/room/metro-1001 (started)
Contact line: +1-415-555-0119 (ops war room)

I’ll update Carla once we have confirmation from the runbook steps.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: MetroHealth — activating AZ1 containment runbook

On it — runbook activated and initial remediation steps executed. Summary: 
- Confirmed KV eviction storm in AZ1 leading to p99 cache thrash and backend timeouts.
- Flows: initiated weighted re-route (60% -> eastus2/westus3 split).
- Edge: increased request concurrency limit on new targets and warmed KV caches via synthetic prefills.
- Autoscale: added two extra inference nodes in westus3 and eastus2; provisioning complete (~5–7m to be ready).

Current status: after weighted shift, aggregate 5xx dropped from 7.5% to 2.1% within 6 minutes; p95 improved to ~480ms but still elevated. Continuing to monitor. If we see <1% 5xx in 10 minutes, we’ll move to 80/20 and then full drain.

Action items outstanding: 
- Hannah: confirm there’s no priority-pin preventing full migration (blocking check).
- Ben: draft comms to MetroHealth with clear rollback and ETA.
- Sean: liaise with MetroHealth execs and confirm approval for potential credits if SLA hit persists.

Attachments: perf-az1-5xx-20281204.png (current), runbook-steps-az1.txt (internal)

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Rodriguez <carla.rodriguez@metrohealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: MetroHealth incident — immediate update

Carla — quick update from the war room: 
- We have started the weighted re-route off AZ1 (60% shifted). Early telemetry shows 5xx halved and p95 reduced.
- We’re provisioning additional inference capacity and performing KV warmup to reduce cache misses.
- We expect stable service in the next 20–30 minutes if trends continue.

Customer ask: we will provide a post-incident timeline and a mitigation plan, plus proposed service credit for impacted minutes should the final SLO analysis show a breach. We’ll aim to keep revenue-impacting credits minimal but fair.

Bridge: https://bluejeans.redwood.ai/room/metro-1001 (ops)
Logs: https://console.redwood.ai/logs?query=metrohealth+az1+2028-12-04

Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: MetroHealth — immediate mitigation in progress (AZ1 routing change)

Carla —

Thanks for the quick call. Short summary for your execs and operations team: 
- What we saw: sudden KV cache thrash and gateway queue growth in AZ1 causing p95 latency and elevated 5xx for MetroHealth traffic.
- What we did: activated AZ1 containment runbook, shifted 60% traffic to eastus2/westus3, provisioned extra inference nodes, performed synthetic cache warmups.
- Current impact: 5xx down to ~1.8% and p95 reduced to ~420–500ms; still above baseline but improving.
- Next steps: continue progressive shift to full drain if error rate does not rebound; post-incident RCA to include timeline, root cause (KV eviction), and compensatory controls (KV autosizing and smarter prefix caching).

Accepting a bridge for the MetroHealth exec team now and will remain on the line until stable. If you want us to fully drain AZ1 immediately we will require explicit approval to complete (there will be a brief rolling warmup window during the shift).

If MetroHealth would like pre-approved remediation concessions, please indicate — we’ll prepare a draft credit proposal while remediation completes.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Leads —

Brief timeline & ask: 
- 08:10 PST: MetroHealth reports spike in 5xx & latency (claims API).
- 08:18 PST: War room opened, runbook activated.
- 08:28 PST: Weighted routing shift initiated (60% off AZ1), provisioning started.
- 08:45 PST: Telemetry improving (5xx down to ~1.8%).
- 10:50 PST: system stable for most flows; ongoing high tail for a subset of claims endpoints.

Customer impact: several high-value hospital partners experienced delayed claims processing for ~30–90 minutes during the peak window. MetroHealth is requesting an expedited SLA credit and a direct exec-level status update.

Ask: approve a provisional customer concession (up to 10% service credit for the affected billing period) so Ben can present an immediate, transparent remediation offer. We’ll finalize after the formal SLO analysis. Also approve a post-incident letter signed by Alex Martinez or the appropriate exec (templates attached).

I recommend we prioritize the relationship — MetroHealth is a strategic account; a swift, empathetic exec response will reduce churn risk.

—Sean
